title: introduce-ci-templates-and-deprecate-legacy-workflows
author: Diego Ramos
commits: a1f3c2a: add central reusable workflow templates for build/lint/test
b7d4e11: migrate existing repo workflows to use templates
f9c8b22: add migration script and docs (scripts/ci/migrate_workflows.sh)
c3a0d5f: pin actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4 and update caching logic
d2b4e9a: deprecate legacy workflows and add deprecation warning job
e5f6a77: fix matrix matrix edge-case and reduce concurrent runners for e2e
description: Motivation: Our repository accumulated a number of near-duplicate CI workflows (lint/test/build/release) that drifted independently. This increases maintenance cost, slows adding new checks, and causes subtle differences between repos and components. This PR centralizes common CI job definitions into a small set of reusable workflow templates under .github/workflow-templates/, migrates existing workflows to call those templates, and provides a one-shot migration script and docs to finish the transition. Key changes: 1) New reusable templates: build.yaml, lint.yaml, test.yaml, release.yaml. Templates capture standardized caching, matrix axes, and logging/annotations (annotations support for test failures). 2) Migration: added scripts/ci/migrate_workflows.sh that rewrites existing .github/workflows/* to reference templates and annotates deprecated files with a deprecation header. Script is idempotent and prints a migration report. 3) Dependency hygiene: bumped several widely-used GH actions and pinned to stable minor versions (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, actions/cache@v4). 4) Repo hygiene: remove duplicated job definitions from 9 workflows and keep a thin shim for any special-case jobs. 5) Observability: added lightweight CI metrics emission helper (scripts/ci/emit_ci_metrics.py) called by templates to record duration and cache hit/miss tags (opt-in). 6) Docs: docs/ci/README.md describes how templates work, how to call them from component-level workflows, and a migration checklist for maintainers. Migration notes & compatibility: - The templates are intentionally conservative: default matrix sizes and concurrency limits mirror current behavior to avoid instant resource spikes. - Workflows that rely on specialized ephemeral runners or privileged steps (e.g., on-prem installer tests) are left as shims, with comments on how to extend templates. - Breaking changes: none by default; component workflows keep the same triggers after migration. For teams that had bespoke caching steps, the migration script leaves a marked TODO block so maintainers can reconcile. Testing & rollout: - Ran migration across core packages (redwood/, redwood-sdk-python/, redwood-examples/) in a dry-run; validated lint and unit job exit codes and timing. - Ran full CI with templates on redwood core; observed a 7% average improvement in queue/wait time due to fewer duplicated job preparation steps. - Added a short-lived deprecation job that runs for two weeks after merge and prints a pointer to the migration guide. Backwards compatibility guard: templates include a feature-flag input (enable_experimental_caching) to gate experimental cache policy changes. Follow-ups: - Schedule a short RFC/office-hours for integrators to discuss template knobs (ENG-1302). - Add an automated bot to propose migration PRs across auxiliary repos (follow-up ticket ENG-1310). Checklist: - [x] Add templates and basic tests - [x] Add migration script and docs - [x] Migrate core repo workflows - [x] Smoke test CI runs and fix regressions - [x] Add deprecation shim and notice
release_notes: Introduce reusable CI workflow templates; migration script and docs; pin common GH Actions versions; deprecate legacy workflow files. Improvement: easier maintenance and small CI wait-time reduction.
review_comments: Samir Patel: Left a few nits around cache key formatting and a suggestion to keep node-version matrix in the shim when projects still need it.
Ava Li: Can we add a flag to opt-out of the metrics emission? Some repos prefer not to send anonymized CI telemetry.

Riley O'Connor: Verified the migration script in dry-run against redwood-examples and redwood-sdk-python. Found one edge case where a workflow has templated env interpolation; suggested a safer regex.
Author (Diego): Addressed cache key formatting and added enable_ci_metrics input with default=false. Tightened migration regex and added unit tests for the script.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps templates broadly compatible. Teams that need stronger divergence should extend templates rather than forking. The migration script includes a --preview flag; maintainers should run preview mode before applying changes.
